You are fixing a real, confirmed layout bug in a YouTube video editing pipeline (Windows, ffmpeg-based). Main script:

C:\Users\edmem\OneDrive\Desktop\Video Projects\first-video\edit\scripts\composite_full.py

Read it in full first — it was recently modified (by a different agent) to redesign `build_webcam_primary()`'s dynamic shrink-aside behavior: for EDL ranges 5 and 18 (webcam_primary ranges carrying a motion-graphic overlay), the webcam now shrinks from full "hero" size to an "ASIDE" size (~60-70% of hero, look for `ASIDE_W`/`ASIDE_H` or similarly named constants) and moves to one side of the screen (right side, `center_x=1455` per that agent's report) while the graphic (`slot_bank_stat` on range 5; `slot_codely_reveal` then `slot_tag_subscribe` on range 18) plays beside it. The neon border scales continuously with the webcam through the whole transition.

## The bug

For range 18's FIRST graphic, `slot_codely_reveal`, the card and the aside-positioned webcam box are placed too close together — their corners visibly touch/overlap. Confirmed via direct frame inspection: `ffmpeg -y -ss 204.0 -i composited_draft.mp4 -vframes 1 frame.png` (204.0s is inside range 18's `codely_reveal` window) shows the card's top-right rounded corner tucked directly under the webcam box's bottom-left rounded corner with essentially zero gap — a real visual collision, not just close spacing. The previous agent's report claimed "real margin" here, which was wrong — verify this yourself with fresh frame extraction before doing anything else, don't just trust either their claim or mine on faith.

For contrast, range 18's SECOND graphic, `slot_tag_subscribe`, is positioned fine (confirmed clear separation from the aside webcam box at t=243.5) — only the `codely_reveal` window has the collision, don't need to touch the subscribe positioning.

## What to check first

`slot_codely_reveal`'s card may have its own internal motion (a reveal/slide animation over its ~3.2s duration) — inspect its HyperFrames source at `C:\Users\edmem\OneDrive\Desktop\Video Projects\first-video\edit\animations\slot_codely_reveal\index.html` and/or extract frames across its FULL window (`rel_start=0.05, dur=3.2` within range 18 -- confirm exact absolute-output-timeline seconds yourself from the current `composited_draft.mp4`/`edl.json`/`OVERLAYS` dict, don't assume t=204.0 is representative of the whole window) to find the card's actual bounding box at multiple points, not just one frame. The fix needs to hold throughout the ENTIRE window, not just avoid collision at t=204.0.

## The fix

Whichever of these actually solves it cleanly (your judgment, verify by extraction either way) — do NOT touch range 5's placement or slot_tag_subscribe's placement, which are both already correct:

- Move the range-18 ASIDE webcam position higher and/or further right so it stays clear of the card's full bounding box throughout the window, OR
- Shrink the range-18 ASIDE size slightly more (still staying within the 60-70%-of-hero band from the original spec — don't go below 60%), OR
- If range 18's two graphics (codely_reveal, tag_subscribe) would genuinely benefit from slightly different ASIDE positions/sizes and the codebase's structure makes that reasonable, do that — but ONLY if a single shared range-18 position genuinely can't achieve clean separation from codely_reveal's full range of motion; prefer one consistent position if achievable, per the original design intent (avoid the webcam visibly hopping between two different positions within one range).

Whatever you land on, this needs REAL margin — not just technically-non-touching by a pixel or two. Aim for a clean, deliberate gap that reads as intentional side-by-side layout, not a near-miss.

## Verification (mandatory)

Sample at least 5-6 frames spread across `slot_codely_reveal`'s ENTIRE window after your fix (not just the start) and confirm genuine clear separation at every sampled point — extract real frames and actually look at them, describe what you see. Then rebuild `seg_18.mp4` (delete and let the script's caching re-trigger it), rebuild `composited_draft.mp4` via `main()`, and rebuild `C:\Users\edmem\OneDrive\Desktop\Video Projects\first-video\edit\mockups\demo_60s_v2.mp4` (check how the previous agent built this — likely a short trimmed-clips-then-concat approach similar to `first-video/edit/highlight_reel/`; reuse the same approach/toggles they used, including `-pix_fmt yuv420p` on every intermediate AND final encode, no grain layer, 25% background scrim — look for `SCRIM_OPACITY`/`include_grain`/`apply_scrim` constants or parameters they added to `build_webcam_primary()`). Confirm the final mockup still decodes cleanly (`ffmpeg -v error -i demo_60s_v2.mp4 -f null -`) and has uniform pix_fmt throughout.

## Deliverable

Fixed `composite_full.py`, rebuilt `seg_18.mp4`, `composited_draft.mp4`, and `demo_60s_v2.mp4`, and a written report: the exact new position/size values, why you chose them, and the specific frames you checked (timestamps + what you saw) proving the fix holds across the graphic's full window. Do not ask clarifying questions.

377	def zoom_filter(z: dict) -> str:
378	    # Supersample before zoompan (4x linear) so the crop window's pixel-rounded
379	    # position error shrinks proportionally at output res -- this is what
380	    # actually kills the end-of-ramp "vibration": zoompan rounds x/y to whole
381	    # *input* pixels each frame, and near the top of an ease-out curve many
382	    # consecutive frames have nearly-but-not-quite-identical zoom, so the
383	    # rounded crop position dithers by +/-1px at the sampling resolution.
384	    # At 4x input res, that same 1px dither is a quarter-output-pixel: gone.
385	    # Rounding the zoom value itself to 4 decimals removes the sub-pixel
386	    # floating-point noise that was driving the dither in the first place.
387	    fps = 60
388	    rsf = z["rs"] * fps
389	    rdf = z["rd"] * fps
390	    cx, cy, Z = z["cx"] * 2, z["cy"] * 2, z["z"]  # cx/cy given in 1x source coords; input is prescaled 2x here
391	    in_ease = f"(1-pow(1-min(max((on-{rsf})/{rdf}\\,0)\\,1)\\,3))"
392	    if z.get("out_rs") is not None:
393	        orsf = z["out_rs"] * fps
394	        ordf = z["out_rd"] * fps
395	        out_ease = f"(1-min(max((on-{orsf})/{ordf}\\,0)\\,1))"
396	        raw_zoom = f"1+({Z}-1)*{in_ease}*{out_ease}"
397	    else:
398	        raw_zoom = f"1+({Z}-1)*{in_ease}"
399	    zoom_expr = f"round(({raw_zoom})*2000)/2000"
400	    x_expr = f"min(max({cx}-(iw/zoom/2)\\,0)\\,iw-iw/zoom)"
401	    y_expr = f"min(max({cy}-(ih/zoom/2)\\,0)\\,ih-ih/zoom)"
402	    zp = f"zoompan=z='{zoom_expr}':x='{x_expr}':y='{y_expr}':d=1:s=1920x1080:fps={fps}"
403	    return f"scale=3840:2160:flags=lanczos,{zp}"

435	def _shrink_u_expr(graphic_start: float, graphic_end: float, td: float) -> str:
436	    """0..1 blend factor for the webcam hero<->corner shrink-aside: 0 = full
437	    hero size/position, 1 = settled corner size/position. Ramps 0->1 (ease-out
438	    cubic) over `td` seconds ending exactly at graphic_start (so the shrink
439	    completes right as the graphic's own CRT entrance begins), holds at 1 for
440	    the graphic's whole window, then ramps back 1->0 over `td` seconds
441	    starting at graphic_end. Same min(ease_in,ease_out) shape as
442	    crt_transition_filter's s_expr, just inverted (0 at the edges instead of
443	    the middle is what we want here since 0 = hero/full-frame, matching s=1
444	    there -- so this reuses s_expr as-is: s=1 in the hold matches u=1 here)."""
445	    ws, we = graphic_start - td, graphic_end + td
446	    p_in = f"min(max((t-{ws})/{td}\\,0)\\,1)"
447	    p_out = f"min(max(({we}-t)/{td}\\,0)\\,1)"
448	    ease_in = f"(1-pow(1-{p_in}\\,3))"
449	    ease_out = f"(1-pow(1-{p_out}\\,3))"
450	    return f"min({ease_in}\\,{ease_out})"

453	def _hero_transform(idx: int, windows: list[tuple[float, float]], td: float = SHRINK_DUR) -> dict:
454	    """Piecewise scale(w,h)/position(x,y) expressions for the webcam feed,
455	    blending between the hero-stage size/position and this range's
456	    ASIDE_CENTER size/position across one or more graphic windows (see
457	    _shrink_u_expr). Multiple windows combine via max() (they don't overlap
458	    in time)."""
459	    cx, cy = ASIDE_CENTER[idx]
460	    aside_x, aside_y = cx - ASIDE_W / 2, cy - ASIDE_H / 2
461	    u_terms = [_shrink_u_expr(gs, ge, td) for gs, ge in windows]
462	    u_expr = u_terms[0]
463	    for term in u_terms[1:]:
464	        u_expr = f"max({u_expr}\\,{term})"
465	    w_expr = f"(2*round(({HERO_W}+({ASIDE_W}-{HERO_W})*{u_expr})/2))"
466	    h_expr = f"(2*round(({HERO_H}+({ASIDE_H}-{HERO_H})*{u_expr})/2))"
467	    x_expr = f"({HERO_X}+({aside_x}-{HERO_X})*{u_expr})"
468	    y_expr = f"({HERO_Y}+({aside_y}-{HERO_Y})*{u_expr})"
469	    return dict(w=w_expr, h=h_expr, x=x_expr, y=y_expr, u=u_expr)

477	    webcam feed enlarged to ~980px tall (its native 4:3 aspect preserved,

481	    webcam+border ASIDE to that range's ASIDE_CENTER (60-70% of hero size,

483	    content), eased, while that range's own graphic overlay(s) are on screen
484	    (see OVERLAYS[idx] + _hero_transform), holding there for the graphic's
485	    window before easing back to hero size. The neon border scales/repositions
486	    continuously in lockstep with the webcam throughout (not just at the two
487	    settled endpoints) -- see the border_dyn block below.
488	    The rounded-corner mask (pip_mask.png) is scaled in lockstep with the
489	    webcam feed itself (same w/h expressions) so the corner radius scales
490	    proportionally with the box at every point in the animation, hero size,
491	    corner size, and everywhere in between.

496	    latest direction, still going back and forth on it) and a background
497	    scrim ON. `apply_scrim` darkens the RAW retrowave background plate only
498	    (via colorchannelmixer, equivalent to alpha-compositing a flat black
499	    layer at SCRIM_OPACITY opacity: out = src*(1-SCRIM_OPACITY)), same
500	    layering principle as the existing grain fix above -- applied to the
501	    background before the border/webcam/graphic are drawn on top, so it
502	    never darkens the presenter or the graphics, only the plate behind them.
503	    """
504	    dur = end - start
505	    overlays = OVERLAYS.get(idx)
506	    dynamic = idx in DYNAMIC_SHRINK_RANGES and overlays
507	
508	    bg_args = ["-stream_loop", "-1", "-i", str(RETROWAVE_BG)]
509	    grain_args = ["-stream_loop", "-1", "-c:v", "libvpx-vp9", "-i", str(GRAIN_LOOP)]
510	    border_args = ["-stream_loop", "-1", "-c:v", "libvpx-vp9", "-i", str(NEON_BORDER)]

525	    # Blank transparent canvas, full 1920x1080 frame size, used only in the
526	    # dynamic-shrink case (see below) as the fixed-size base that the

528	    # independent uses via split=2 -- the border does NOT use this canvas,
529	    # see the border_dyn note below). MUST be the full frame (not just
530	    # HERO_W x HERO_H) -- the aside box (e.g. range 5's, up to x=1880,y=859)

540	
541	    # Optional scrim (see apply_scrim docstring note above), then grain/
